subject: Deploy model fit and migration scoping
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver@brightscale.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightscale.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: deployment preferences and migration constraints

Tessa — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Sara and I captured a few follow-ups and wanted to confirm a couple of details before we map internal stakeholders. High level: we're evaluating three options but leaning away from fully self-hosted due to ops headcount. Notes/questions: 

- Current production setup: primarily using another LLM API provider (we call it "VendorX"). We have a small legacy GPU cluster (on-prem) for batch jobs.
- Traffic profile: 800–1,200 QPS spikes for short windows (ad hoc), baseline ~120 QPS. Typical generation length ~300 tokens.
- Data residency: must remain in us-west for now; later EU expansion in H2.
- Security: will request SOC2 + network diagrams and KMS options.

We're trying to decide between: 
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, but we need clarity on egress/data retention and VPC egress for sensitive payloads.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): attractive if we can get predictable latency during spikes and commit to a quarter.
- Private VPC / on-prem: possible but would be a heavier integration — we'd prefer Redwood to outline migration effort and lockstep plan.

Immediate asks from our side: 
1) Can you provide a short matrix that maps: effort to onboard, estimated lead time, typical latency range, and cost delta (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for our traffic profile?
2) If we migrate from VendorX, what are common pitfalls (prompt/response TTF, tokenization differences, embedding drift)?

Attaching our high-level traffic snapshot (pdf) and a quick columnar matrix we use internally. If you can send a recommended next-step plan for each mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and an estimated timeline, we can route to procurement and infra.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Chen
Head of AI Platforms
BrightScale Analytics

Attachments: migration-snapshot-2027Q1.pdf (summary), traffic-sample.csv (referenced but not attached in this thread)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@brightscale.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightscale.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment preferences and migration constraints

Oliver / Sara — great to meet you both. Short recap and concrete next steps below so we have a single plan to share with your procurement/infra teams. I pulled in Aditya (product) and Marcus (solutions engineering) for technical/contract items.

Quick summary of options (one-liners):
- Hosted API: fastest to production (days). Good for early validation; supports streaming, function calls, and our standard retention/egress controls. Can add routed VPC egress + token-level redaction rules for sensitive workloads.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in us-west with predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit. Ideal if you need sustained low-latency and can commit to a quarterly/annual block.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration. Longer lead time (weeks to a few months) but required if policy/regulation demands no shared control plane.

Requested deliverables from Redwood (we will provide these this week):
1) Deployment choice matrix (effort / lead time / latency / cost delta) — see attached xlsx.
2) Migration checklist from typical LLM APIs (tokenization, prompt framing, eval pass rates, embedding parity) — 1-page.
3) Draft mutual action plan template (owners, milestones, gating items) to hand to procurement.

Proposed next steps and timing:
- Today: sending the deployment-choice-matrix.xlsx and short migration-snapshot pdf (attached).
- Wed, Feb 17: 30-min technical deep-dive with Marcus to validate latency and batching assumptions (I propose 10:00am PT).
- Fri, Feb 19: procurement kickoff with Aditya (pricing and contract template).

Can you confirm that those dates work and that we should include your security contact on the Wed call? Also confirm whether you want Redwood to run a short 48‑hour spike test against a dedicated pool (we can scope cost/size once we validate peak QPS).

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: deployment-choice-matrix.xlsx (estimates)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@brightscale.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment preferences and migration constraints

Oliver — quick technical notes ahead of Wednesday's deep-dive. I pulled sample numbers against a similar profile last quarter for a fintech customer and wanted to flag a few migration items so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted correctly: 

1) Tokenization/embedding parity: vendor differences typically show up in embeddings and sometimes prompt truncation. We'll run an embedding parity job and a small eval set (50 prompts) as part of initial validation — should take <48 hours.
2) KV cache warm-up and batching: for short spikes you get much better p99 if we pre-warm caches and use continuous batching (we can automate warm-ups during scheduled spike windows).
3) Routing & fallback: recommended pattern — primary: Dedicated in us-west; fallback: Hosted in us-west (cheaper, burstable). For Sensitive flows we can enable VPC egress-only routes to your KMS and set a retention override.
4) Migration gotchas: prompt templating differences (model-specific tokens), streaming chunk sizes that break parsers, and differences in stop token behavior. We'll include tooling to normalize streaming responses.

For the 48-hour spike test: we can provision a 4-GPU dedicated pool in us-west, run a 72-hour soak with controlled ramp to your peak, and gather p50/p90/p99 and unit cost. I'll scope an estimate for Wednesday.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightscale.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment preferences and migration constraints

Tessa / team — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of quick clarifications from procurement/security: 

- Security questionnaire: we'll send the initial one by EOD today. Please confirm who on your side will be the point for security evidence (Diagrams, SOC2 artifacts, KMS attestations).
- Purchasing cadence: we prefer a single PO + one quarter evaluation. If Dedicated shows measurable latency improvement, we'll explore annual commit.
- Spike test: yes to the 48/72 hour soak. Please add estimated cost/credit arrangements for that test.

If you can send the migration checklist and the high-level per-token delta by EOD Wed, we will route to procurement and book the Wed deep-dive with our infra and security leads.

Sara Patel
Director of Procurement | BrightScale Analytics
